title: Constructible module subsheaves over Noetherian rings
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $\Lambda$ a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For a monomorphism $F\to G$ of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], if $G$ is constructible [def-constructible-constructible], then $F$ is constructible in the same finitely generated module sense. No torsion or finite-ring hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09BH, Proposition 59.74.1 (3), proof of (3); Tag 095E. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RY.

proof.text: Apply Noetherian induction on closed subsets of X. Exact inverse image retains the inclusion of the first term into the middle term. By generic constancy and an etale trivialization, work near each component generic point with a constant middle sheaf of a finitely generated module M on an irreducible scheme.

Its generic submodule N is finitely generated because the coefficient ring is Noetherian. Lift a finite generating set to a common pointed etale neighbourhood. The images of the lifts are constant, so their two pullbacks agree; monicity and the sheaf condition descend the lifts to the open image. The constant N is now contained in the first term. Membership in a subobject of a constant sheaf is open, and every nonempty open of an irreducible scheme meets its generic point; consequently this inclusion is equality. Descent produces a finite locally constant first term on a nonempty open of each component.

Repeat on the proper closed complement. Noetherian induction yields a finite locally closed stratification for the first term. Every locally closed part of a Noetherian space is constructible, so this is IsConstructibleSheaf in the source library.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09BH, Proposition 59.74.1 (3), proof of (3); Tag 095E. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RY.
